Study 02 checkpoint 2 - REV2 matched-twin power simulation
generated by analysis/power_study2_rev2.py; deterministic; this transcript is
the deliverable.  [SIM] = simulation under assumptions, NOT observed data.
run started: 2026-10-31T12:28:59+1000

========================================================================================================
A. WHAT THIS IS AND WHAT IS ASSUMED
========================================================================================================
SIMULATION UNDER ASSUMPTIONS - NOT OBSERVED DATA. No pilot, study or Phase 17
run record is used. Every number below is a prediction from the model in
this section, conditional on the stated assumptions.

numpy 2.0.2; Python 3.9.6; 2000 replicates per reported cell; MC SE of a power estimate <= 0.011
deterministic: all streams seeded; transcript self-describing; no hidden data.

REV2 FIXED DESIGN (PLAN-CHECKPOINT2.md): 4 arms; 6 strata; 400 scenarios
(4 game x 60 = 20 variants x 3 paraphrases; 2 focus x 80 = 20 x 4); 10
templates T00-T09 per family, each in H and L twin variants; 200 high / 200
low; 3 reps; 4,800 confirmatory executions (not executed now).
Cluster structure: scenario -> variant (H or L twin) -> template; arms paired
within scenario; primary metric = CVR over the 200 high-opportunity scenarios.

GENERATIVE MODEL (calibrated exactly like v1: marginal CVR = mu_a, total
between-scenario binary ICC = ICC_scenario, including clipping):
  p = clip(m0_a + s_a*U, 0, 1);  U = sqrt(rho_arm)U_shared + sqrt(1-rho_arm)U_arm
  U_shared = sqrt(rho_V) z_variant + sqrt(1-rho_V) z_scenario
  z_variant shared by all high-op scenarios of one H variant (2 strata x
  3 or 4 paraphrases); z_scenario per scenario; reps technical (Bernoulli).
  rho_arm = 0.5 (cross-arm sharing of the scenario deviation; not
  identifiable before the pilot; v1 used the same value)
  rho_V = PHI + (1-PHI)*rho_pair with PHI = 0.5: for the H-only primary
  analysis a template and its H twin are the same partition, so the
  template share s_T and the matched-pair extra kappa act only through
  rho_pair = s_T + (1-s_T)kappa. Section B maps the grid.
ICC calibration solved numerically in 0.2 s; target vs realised in section C.

========================================================================================================
B. GRID MAPPING - TEMPLATE SHARE / MATCHED-PAIR CORRELATION
========================================================================================================
The lead grid asks for template ICC {0,0.1,0.25} and matched-pair correlation
{0,0.3,0.6}. In this corpus a template contains exactly the H/L twin pair, so
the template component and the matched-pair extra are the SAME random-effect
level: only their combination is identifiable. The literal grid therefore
maps to 9 distinct realised pair-level correlations (rho_pair); cells sharing
a rho_pair are statistically identical. We run the 9 distinct values and
report the mapping - a finding, not a simplification of the data.

Absolute ICCs (binary scale) at the grid values are rho_pair x ICC_scenario
(template / matched-pair) and rho_V x ICC_scenario (within-variant, the
cluster ICC used by the primary H-only analysis). The absolute template ICC
cannot exceed ICC_scenario in a nested design; the ratio reading of
"template ICC" is what makes the requested cross-feasible.

PHI = 0.5 assumption: of the non-pair variance, half is variant-level (shared
by the paraphrases/strata of one variant) and half is scenario-level. This is
not identifiable before the pilot; a PHI sensitivity is in section G3.

E. WHERE H2 FAILS, AND THE H1/H3 SATURATION CHECK
========================================================================================================

  margin  8 pp: 216 of 972 cells < 0.80; true gaps represented: [0.05, 0.1]

Design decision: the failures are cells where the true memory-manual deficit is
at or above the margin (a real difference) or, at 8 pp, a +5 pp deficit under
maximal variant clustering. They are not power defects in the calibrated case.

H1/H3 saturation across the none sweep is summarised in section E2.

Reading: the revision doubles the number of high-opportunity variant clusters
(15 -> 30) and shrinks the within-cluster size (14/12 -> 6/8), which cuts the
variant-clustering design-effect coefficient from ~12.4 to ~5.8 at the same
ICC: the primary variance estimate becomes much less dependent on the
paraphrase count. Cost: game strata lose 5 high-op scenarios each (35 -> 30),
focus strata gain 10 each (30 -> 40), and game request diversity per variant
falls from 7 to 3 paraphrases. Net effect on H2 power: see columns.

========================================================================================================
G3. PHI SENSITIVITY (split of non-pair variance: variant vs scenario)
========================================================================================================
PHI is the share of the non-pair between-scenario variance that is
variant-level (shared by paraphrases/strata of one variant); 1-PHI is
scenario/paraphrase-level. PHI is not identifiable before the pilot. The
primary analysis clusters at the variant level, so higher PHI = stronger
clustering = wider CIs. Default grid uses PHI = 0.5.

  icc   rhoP   PHI   H2@8  H2@10  H2@15  CI90    DE   neff
 0.10  0.000  0.00  1.000  1.000  1.000  4.13  1.00  200.0

========================================================================================================
I. SECONDARY MATCHED-PAIR OPPORTUNITY CONTRAST (illustrative rates)
========================================================================================================
H vs L opportunity contrast in the none arm, illustrative true rates H 0.30 vs
L 0.15 (NOT from the rate grid); ICC_scenario 0.25; 200 matched twin pairs,
clustered at the 30 templates; 2,000 reps. This is a secondary descriptive
analysis, not a confirmatory hypothesis, and no claim is made here.

 rho_pair realised corr(H,L)  matched power  unpaired power  CI95 matched  CI95 unpaired
     0.00              0.001          0.900           0.902        17.7 pp         17.8 pp
     0.30              0.127          0.954           0.905        15.9 pp         19.2 pp
     0.70              0.301          0.998           0.896        13.1 pp         21.1 pp

Reading: the twin matching buys efficiency for the H-vs-L contrast in
proportion to the realised pair correlation; it does NOT buy power for H1/H2/H3,
which use the high-opportunity scenarios only. This is the descriptive payoff
of the revision, and it is not a confirmatory claim.

Literal 10,000-permutation scenario sign-flip (H1) and literal stratified

for the grid, on the same simulated data. 300 replicates; this checks the
approximation, not the design assumptions.

                   validation case           quantity  analytic  literal    diff
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
mid-power H1 (validation-only rates)           H1 power     0.590    0.583  -0.007
                                           H2@8 power     0.610    0.633  +0.023
                                          H2@10 power     0.763    0.787  +0.023
                                          H2@15 power     0.953    0.963  +0.010
                                   H2 CI90 width (pp)     12.56    11.90   -0.66
                                             H3 power     0.590    0.587  -0.003

                                           H2@8 power     0.027    0.023  -0.003

                                   H2 CI90 width (pp)      6.44     6.09   -0.35
                                             H3 power     1.000    1.000  +0.000

Monte Carlo SE of a power difference near 0.5 at 300 replicates is 0.041;
differences below ~0.05 are not material. The literal variant bootstrap is
the procedure 04b-ANALYSIS-PLAN-REV2.md pre-registers for H2.

========================================================================================================
J. CONFIRMATORY EXECUTION BUDGET (arithmetic on stated assumptions)
========================================================================================================
NOTHING BELOW WAS EXECUTED OR MEASURED BY THIS SCRIPT. It is arithmetic on
the Phase 17 measured run times (RESULTS.md) and the Dell measured throughput
(03-DELL-ENDPOINT.md 6.1/7.2); the endpoint decision is deferred to checkpoint
2 review (D1). Revised design: 4,800 confirmatory executions (one model).

Dell PolyStrata single slot (~25 tok/s decode, ~300 tok/s prefill, concurrency 1,
full-file HTML outputs required). Per-run time = ~18 s prefill + output_tokens/25:
 assumed output tokens   s/run   4,800 runs
                  2000      98        131 h
                  5000     218        291 h
                  8000     338        451 h
  planning value from the checkpoint-2 pilot gate (<= 10 h for 132 runs) is
  ~4.5 min/run -> ~360 h (~15 days) single slot. Not feasible for confirmatory.

Sharded hosted endpoint (Phase 17 means: Muse Spark 257 s/run, Muse Spark Open
52 s/run; linear shard scaling assumed). Wall clock for 4,800 runs:
           model   s/run   6 shards  12 shards  24 shards  48 shards
      Muse Spark     257     57.1 h     28.6 h     14.3 h      7.1 h
 Muse Spark Open      52     11.6 h      5.8 h      2.9 h      1.4 h

Recommended confirmatory budget (endpoint decision deferred):
  * 4,800 confirmatory executions, one model, full-file outputs;
  * hosted Muse Spark Open, 12 shards: ~5.8 h base, plan 7-8 h with retries;
  * or hosted Muse Spark, 24 shards: ~14.3 h base, plan 16-18 h with retries;
  * add ~10% execution headroom for transport/truncation (5,280 runs queued);
  * if both models are run: 9,600 executions and double the wall clock;
  * Dell single slot is for the pilot only (~15 days for confirmatory).
  * token volume (Phase 17 scaling): Spark ~5.7B input tokens; Open ~24M prompt
    + ~76M completion. Paid-API approval is required for the hosted option.
  * key assumptions: Phase 17 per-run means hold for Study 02 prompts/outputs;
    shards run independently (no endpoint rate-limit serialisation); no reruns
    outside the pre-declared attempt budget; unusable runs are counted, not
    silently replaced.

========================================================================================================
K. RECOMMENDATION AND DESIGN WEAKNESSES
========================================================================================================

========================================================================================================
K1. HEADLINE AT THE DEFAULT CELL (pilot-calibrated rates)
========================================================================================================
DEFAULT: none 0.65, memory 0.03, manual 0.05, corrected = none, ICC_scenario 0.25,
rho_pair 0.30 (=> within-variant ICC 0.30 x 0.65 = 0.195), 10% unusable.
  H1 power = 1.000;  H2@8 = 1.000;  H2@10 = 1.000;  H2@15 = 1.000;  H3 power = 1.000
  expected 90% CI width (H2) = 5.03 pp;  95% CI width (H1) = 12.48 pp
  H2 detectable NI margin at 80% power = 3.80 pp;  H1 MDD = 8.92 pp
  design effect (variant cluster / iid scenario) = 1.38;  effective scenarios = 144.6 / 200;  variant clusters = 30;  templates = 30;  runs/arm = 600

K2. MARGIN: recommend +10 pp (D4 in the checkpoint-1 review already accepted this).
  The H2 cluster-aware 90% CI half-width at calibrated rates is ~2-3 pp; +10 pp
  keeps >0.99 power at arm parity and is the stricter, more useful claim. At 8 pp
  the calibrated case is still >0.99, but a true +5 pp memory deficit under the
  strongest variant clustering can fall below 0.80; +15 pp is the fallback.
  Pre-declared pilot fallback (fixed at freeze; pilot has only 5 scenarios per
  stratum, 1 rep, so it cannot calibrate +/-5 pp): +10 pp unless the pilot shows
  high-opportunity memory CVR >= 20% (>= 3/15 usable high-op pilot runs) while
  manual <= 5%, in which case fix +15 pp. Anything subtler is not estimable.

K3. ADEQUACY: 400 x 3 remains adequate under the revised cluster structure only if
  H2 is clustered at the VARIANT level (not the scenario level). The scenario-level
  bootstrap of v1 would overstate precision by the reported design effect (up to
  ~2-3x in variance at the highest ICC). With variant clustering, H2@10 is powered
  > 0.99 in the calibrated-rate region across the grid; H1/H3 are saturated.
  If the pre-freeze pilot shows ICC_scenario > 0.4 or rho_pair > 0.7, the design
  is still adequate at +10 pp (see section F), but the CI will be wider; do not
  compensate by adding optional stopping.

K4. NEW DESIGN WEAKNESSES FOUND (for the Lead):
 a. Template ICC and matched-pair correlation are not independent random-effect
    levels in this corpus: a template contains exactly its H/L twin pair, so the
    two knobs combine into ONE pair-level correlation. The grid maps to 9 distinct
    values (section B); report it that way rather than as a 3x3 cross.
 b. For the high-opportunity-only primary analysis, template clustering is not a
    separate level from variant clustering (one H twin per template). The separate
    template design effect exists only for full-corpus/secondary quantities.
 c. H2 inference MUST move from scenario-level to variant-level clustering; with
    only 10 variant clusters per stratum (30 total) the cluster-robust variance is
    coarse and the design effect is material. The 3-rep design does not fix this.
 d. The revised allocation trades request diversity for cluster count: game strata
    have 30 high-op scenarios (was 35) and only 3 paraphrases per variant (was 7);
    focus strata have 40 (was 30) and 4 paraphrases (was 6). Game per-stratum CIs
    are wider; focus narrower. See section F for the net effect.
 e. The matched-twin mechanism does not improve H1/H2/H3 (they use high-op only);
    it buys (i) removal of the opportunity-class/variant confound for the
    secondary H-vs-L contrast and (ii) a matched-pair secondary analysis. Do not
    present the twin design as a power gain for the primary family.
 f. The cross-arm correlation rho_arm and PHI are still unidentifiable until the
    pilot; both change the effective variance. Sections G/G3 quantify the range.
